University Academic Regulations Framework 2026-2027 - Page 1
Category: Academic Regulations | Section 1.1 Degree Requirements and Credit Load
Full-time undergraduate students must register for a minimum of 12
credits and a maximum of 18 credits per standard semester.
Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA) of 2.0 on a 4.0 scale is
mandatory for maintaining Good Academic Standing and conferral of
degree.
Students falling below a 2.0 CGPA at the close of any semester are
placed on Academic Notice for the subsequent active academic period.

University Academic Regulations Framework 2026-2027 - Page 2
Category: Academic Regulations | Section 2.4 Grading Policy and Resolution Deadlines
Letter grades are awarded from A (4.00), B (3.00), C (2.00), D (1.00)
through F (0.00). An Incomplete grade (I) is temporary and granted
only under documented extenuating circumstances.
All Incomplete grades must be resolved by the student and certifying
faculty no later than six weeks into the following semester.
Unresolved grades automatically convert to F.

University Academic Regulations Framework 2026-2027 - Page 3
Category: Academic Regulations | Section 3.2 Add Drop Deadlines and Withdrawal
Courses dropped within the initial ten instructional days of the term
do not appear on official student transcripts.
Course withdrawals filed between the third week and the tenth week
receive a permanent mark of W. No withdrawals are authorized after
week ten except via Formal Dean Petition.

pages.text:
Institutional Attendance and Participation Policy - Page 1
Category: Attendance Policy | Section 4.1 Minimum Attendance Standards
Regular attendance and engagement in scheduled instructional sessions
are required for all registered undergraduate and graduate courses.
Students must maintain a minimum attendance of 75 percent in each
enrolled lecture and seminar course to be eligible to sit for final
semester examinations.
Failure to achieve the required 75 percent minimum attendance without
Dean-sanctioned excused absence documentation leads to an
administrative Grade of FA (Failure for Non-Attendance).

Institutional Attendance and Participation Policy - Page 2
Category: Attendance Policy | Section 5.3 Medical and Official Institutional Absences
Documented illness, university-sponsored athletic competitions, or
official jury duty qualify for Excused Absence consideration.
Official medical certificates from a licensed healthcare provider
must be submitted to the Student Affairs Office within five business
days following the student return to campus.
Faculty members must afford students with verified excused absences a
reasonable opportunity to complete missed graded coursework or
designated equivalency assessments.

ACADEMIC POLICY

Applicability: Alliance School of Business

Attendance & DSA requirement for eligibility to Semester End Examination

A student must have secured the minimum attendance in every single subject of a particular semester. A student must also have secured the minimum During Semester Assessment (DSA) marks in a subject to qualify to take the Semester End Examination (SEE). In the event a student falls short of the minimum attendance requirement or/and minimum DSA marks requirement in any subject(s) of the semester, the student is disqualified to take the SEE of that subject(s). The student, however, can take the SEE of the particular subject(s) for a total of 100% of marks after six months.

Evaluation of Industry Internship Program / Project Work / Dissertation

A student must have secured a minimum of 50% component marks (which is 35 out of 70 marks) to qualify to take Viva-voce. Further, the student should secure a minimum of 50% in Viva-voce (which is 15 out of 30 marks) to get pass grade.

In the event a student falls short of minimum component / Viva-voce marks requirement in Industry Internship Program / Project Work / Dissertation, the student has to register in next cycle of re-examination and resubmit the updated Internship Report / Project Work / Dissertation.

In the event a student has not completed his Industry Internship Program of eight to ten weeks, the student has to repeat Industry Internship Program in the succeeding year, whereas if a student has not completed the Project Work / Dissertation, the student has to repeat Project Work / Dissertation in the succeeding re-examination cycle.

Assessment shall be through continuous evaluation and the marks for the same shall be distributed in the following manner:

Provided that, in the event a student falls short of the attendance requirement, the student will be declared as 'I' (Incomplete) for that paper.
